name: Betawi

ancestors.notes: Malay lexifier: Betawi is a Malay-derived creoloid that formed among the mixed population of colonial-era Batavia; the bulk of its vocabulary and grammar continues Low Malay (Grijns 1991, Jakarta Malay: Its History and Its Kinship with Malay Dialects).

Javanese substrate: migrants from Central/East Java were a major component of Batavia's mixed founder population and contributed vocabulary and phonological features to Betawi (Ikranagara 1980, Muysken & Grijns literature on Jakarta Malay/Betawi genesis).
Sundanese substrate: West Javanese (Sundanese-speaking) population contact around Batavia, cited alongside Javanese in the standard Betawi-formation accounts (Grijns 1991).
Dutch adstrate: three centuries of Batavia/Jakarta colonial administration (VOC then Dutch East Indies) left loanwords in Betawi vocabulary.

notes: Betawi (Betawi Malay / basa Betawi) — Malayic (Austronesian) creole-influenced language of Jakarta, Indonesia. Written in the Latin script following Indonesian orthographic conventions. GRAPHEME INVENTORY NOT YET SPECIFIED: Betawi has no codified standard orthography of its own and its phonology is not documented to a level that supports a reliable letter→phoneme table here. INPUT CONTRACT: input is expected in the Latin script, spelled per Indonesian conventions. wikidata_qid left unset: the code's Wikidata row resolves to the Wikimedia project item, not the language item; not recorded rather than record a wrong id. ANCESTRY: Malay (ms) lexifier with Javanese (jv)/Sundanese (su) substrate influence and a Dutch (nl) adstrate loanword layer, per Grijns (1991) and Ikranagara (1980); Hokkien Chinese contact is also reported in the literature but has no spec in this registry, so is left unwired (see PR notes).
